title: Dimi bar Kakuzta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Shabbat 156a, Rav Ashi said: “Dimi bar Kakuzta and I were born on a Sunday”—Hyman explains, “we were born on the same day”—“I became a leader [literally, a king], while he became the chief of thieves.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Talmud says both were born on a Sunday; “on the same day” is Hyman’s explanatory parenthesis. “King” is used here for leadership. The heading spells קקוזתא while the quotation spells קקוזטא; both underlying forms remain preserved.

The actual Shabbat 156a paragraph names Rav Ashi and Dimi bar Kakozta, with Sunday, king and chief of thieves. “On the same day” remains Hyman’s gloss; king is retained with its leadership sense rather than treated as a new political office claim.
